topics.topic: Semantics of source_id and size when a file is rejected after partial or repeated byte reads
questions: If a file is rejected after some or all of its bytes were read, must `source_id` contain the hash of those bytes, or must it still be absent because every `rejected` observation has no `source_id`?

Is `size` the length of the logical byte sequence hashed into `source_id`, or the cumulative number of bytes read from the file, including repeated reads; and what corresponding rule applies when a rejected observation has no `source_id`?
Does “before its bytes were read” mean before any byte was read or before all bytes were read, and therefore what is `size` when reading succeeds only for a prefix before the file is rejected?

quotes:
What one scan saw for one file of the photo folder. A placed file adds its `file_ref`, a published
file adds its Portal `photo_id`, and files with the same content carry the same `source_id`. The
deliverer computes it on each scan; the calling flow reads it. A server path is never part of it. `size`
is the number of bytes that were read, the bytes `source_id` is the hash of; a file rejected before its
bytes were read has the size its metadata gave when it was listed. `source_id` is present for `ready`, `placed` and
`published` and absent for `rejected`, `reason` is present only for `rejected`, `file_ref` for `placed`
and `published`, and `photo_id` only for `published`.
judgement.why: The passage makes source_id absent for every rejected observation, defines size from the logical bytes read and hashed rather than cumulative I/O, and uses metadata size only when rejection occurs before any bytes are read, so a partially read rejection reports the prefix length.
